supplementaryReferences.note: Wild olive is distinct from a named commercial olive cultivar. March–July describes fruit following flowers; no exact ripe-picking start/end is established.

care: SANBI records this slow-growing tree in summer and winter rainfall areas, with frost, drought and wind resistance.
Keep its roots away from walls, patios and pools; SANBI notes that they can be aggressive.
purchase: Ask for the wild-olive taxon in the catalogue, rather than substituting a commercial olive cultivar. Record actual local picking.
